app.title: CV Zebrafish web prototype: fin and tail kinematics from a pose-tracking CSV
app.summary: The person picks a species, then uploads one pose-tracking CSV, or uses the bundled sample, with an optional config that names the body points. The file is checked, its body parts are matched against the config, and the kinematic calculations run. The results page shows a summary table of the main measurements and a fin-angle and tail-distance plot that a frame-range slider narrows. Below that is the full per-frame results table, and the person downloads the results as a CSV.

task.text: Turn one pose-tracking file into per-frame fin, tail and head kinematics, look over them, and download the results table.

data.text: A tracked-pose table with x, y and likelihood for each named body point in every video frame, plus a JSON config that maps body points to anatomy and sets the analysis parameters.
data.item: a video frame of one tracked animal

stage.text: analysing pose-tracking output after markerless tracking, before plotting and reporting

mechanism.text: A sidebar shows the steps (Species, Load, Results). Each page unlocks the next one: the analysis runs as soon as a file is loaded. On the results page, a range slider redraws the time-series plot for the chosen frames, and the summary, plot, full table and download sit one above the other.

field.text: kinematic analysis of markerless pose-tracking data in animal behaviour

workflow.name: compute derived measures from one tracked recording and export them

steps.step: choose the kind of subject, which sets the analysis path
steps.here: a Species dropdown with Continue sends zebrafish to the analysis and mouse to a placeholder page
upload a DeepLabCut CSV or press 'Use the bundled sample file'; an optional config JSON can be uploaded under 'Config (optional)'

steps.step: check the input against the expected structure before computing
steps.here: the CSV is checked for its format, and body parts named in the config but missing from the file stop the run with a list of both

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: fin angles, tail distance, head yaw, spine angles and swim bouts are computed for every frame
a table gives the unit, mean, min and max of the main measurements

steps.step: narrow the plot to one period
steps.here: a 'Frame range' slider redraws the fin-angle and tail-distance plot for the chosen frames
the full per-frame results open in an expander, and 'Download results CSV' saves them

distinctive: the analysis is driven by a config that maps tracked point names to anatomy (fins, head, spine, tail), so the same code serves different tracking set-ups
a mismatch between the config's body parts and the file's stops the run instead of returning empty results
the measurements are angles and distances relative to the body's own axis, computed for every video frame
the slider's default range comes from the config's first time range
